# RORORO Mac — Threat Model

## What this is

RORORO Mac is a Mac-native multi-Roblox launcher. It captures and stores Roblox session cookies, breaks the Roblox client's single-instance enforcement via `sem_unlink`, claims the system handler for `roblox-player://`, and (Slope C onward) posts synthetic keyboard + mouse events into Roblox windows. There is no server, no HTTP API, no backend. Everything runs on the user's Mac.

The protected primary asset is the user's Roblox session — specifically the `.ROBLOSECURITY` cookie that grants account access. Secondary assets: the EdDSA private key that signs Sparkle updates (off-machine, in 1Password + GitHub Secrets only), and the user's trust in not having keystrokes injected into the wrong process.

This doc complements [`docs/security-audit.md`](../security-audit.md). The audit is the bullet-point posture statement; this is the STRIDE-shaped enumeration. Where the audit already says something authoritatively, this doc cites rather than duplicates.

## Trust boundaries

| Boundary | Trusted side | Untrusted side |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The user's Mac | Everything inside the login Keychain + the RORORO process | Other user accounts on the same Mac, any other unprivileged process |
| Login Keychain | Items with service `com.626labs.rororo-mac.account-cookie`, encrypted by the OS to the login session | Plaintext disk, iCloud Keychain (`kSecAttrSynchronizable: false`), any other Mac |
| Roblox API surface | `auth.roblox.com`, `users.roblox.com`, `thumbnails.roblox.com` over HTTPS with App Transport Security defaults | Any non-Roblox host. Any plaintext channel |
| Sparkle update channel | The DMG signed with our EdDSA private key; appcast.xml signed end-to-end | The HTTPS transport itself (GitHub Pages CDN). Treat the wire as compromised; rely on EdDSA signature |
| URL-scheme registry | Whatever LaunchServices reports for `roblox-player://` at boot | Any other app that subsequently claims the scheme while RORORO is foreground |
| Accessibility / Input Monitoring TCC grants | The user's explicit per-app grant in System Settings | Apps that pretend to be us. macOS's TCC database is the actual trust root here |
| Per-launch Roblox.app copies | The bytes we copy from `/Applications/Roblox.app` at copy time | Any later modification on disk — copies are not re-verified before spawn |

## What we protect

Ordered by blast radius if compromised.

| Asset | Where it lives | Sensitivity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.ROBLOSECURITY` cookies (multi-account) | Login Keychain, `kSecClassGenericPassword`, service `com.626labs.rororo-mac.account-cookie`, account = Roblox userId | **Critical** — equivalent to the account password; long-lived |
| Sparkle EdDSA private key | 1Password + GitHub Secrets only; never on a user's Mac | **Critical** — compromise = silent malicious updates to every existing client; one-way break per CLAUDE.md |
| Apple Developer ID signing cert + notary credentials | 1Password + GitHub Actions secrets | **Critical** — compromise = sign + notarize anything as 626 Labs |
| URL-scheme handler claim state | UserDefaults — `RORORO.URLSchemeHandler.savedRobloxPlayerHandler` saves the previous handler so we can restore on quit | Medium — losing the saved-previous strand breaks restore, not auth |
| `accounts.json` (Application Support) | Plain JSON — userId, username, displayName, avatar URL, last-launched timestamp | Low — same data Roblox exposes publicly |
| `favorites.json`, `private-servers.json` | Plain JSON in Application Support | Low for favorites; private-server codes are session-class secrets and get redacted in diagnostics bundles ([`DiagnosticsBundle.swift`](../../App/RORORO/Domain/DiagnosticsBundle.swift)) |
| Auto-keys macro library | Application Support JSON, no cookies, no credentials | Low |

## Attack surface

The places untrusted input or untrusted actors meet RORORO code.

- **`WKWebView` at `https://www.roblox.com/login`** — the only place we render external HTML. Non-persistent data store ([`CookieCapture.swift:67`](../../App/RORORO/Domain/CookieCapture.swift)).
- **Roblox API responses** — `auth.roblox.com`, `users.roblox.com`, `thumbnails.roblox.com` over HTTPS. Parsed into typed structs; failures don't block.
- **Sparkle appcast at `https://estevanhernandez-stack-ed.github.io/rororo-mac/appcast.xml`** — EdDSA-verified before any DMG is opened ([`Info.plist` `SUPublicEDKey`](../../App/RORORO/Info.plist)).
- **`roblox-player://` URLs incoming to our handler** — browser-originated, claimed via [`URLSchemeHandler.swift`](../../App/RORORO/Domain/URLSchemeHandler.swift).
- **The user's `/Applications/Roblox.app` bundle** — we copy it per-launch into Application Support and execute the copy. We trust the bytes-at-copy-time; we do not re-verify the original's signature each launch.
- **Accessibility / Input Monitoring event taps** — the safety-monitor reads global `NSEvent` streams ([`EventTapping.swift`](../../App/RORORO/Domain/AutoKeys/EventTapping.swift)).
- **Posted `CGEvent` keystrokes + mouse events** — synthetic events stamped with `eventSourceUserData = 0x524F524F` ("RORO") so we can recognize our own and the safety monitor doesn't trip on them.
- **DMG download path** — GitHub Releases. Compromised CDN ≠ compromised app; Sparkle EdDSA signature is the gate.
- **The Keychain item query surface** — any process on the same login can call `SecItemCopyMatching` with our service + account. macOS access control lists gate this; first read prompts the user once per requesting binary.

## Threats — STRIDE

### Spoofing

| Threat | Vector | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Phishing login page in `WKWebView` | We point the WebView at `https://www.roblox.com/login` directly; no redirector. A DNS-poisoned or CA-compromised attacker could MITM, but App Transport Security pins HTTPS + cert validation defaults | Mitigated by ATS + direct URL ([`CookieCapture.swift`](../../App/RORORO/Domain/CookieCapture.swift)); reviewed in [`docs/security-audit.md`](../security-audit.md) |
| Other-process pretends to be RORORO when reading Keychain items | macOS Keychain access-control lists gate by signed binary identity. A different unsigned binary cannot impersonate us; a different signed binary would still trigger a user prompt on first read | Mitigated by Keychain ACLs + Developer ID signing |
| Malicious app claims `roblox-player://` after we've started, intercepts our launch URLs | LaunchServices is last-write-wins. While RORORO is running we don't re-verify ownership on every launch | **Action item** — `URLSchemeHandler.isClaimed` exists ([`URLSchemeHandler.swift:42`](../../App/RORORO/Domain/URLSchemeHandler.swift)) but isn't called pre-launch on every flow. Cheap to add; track as a v0.1.0 hardening item |
| Fake update package signed by attacker | EdDSA private key off-machine; compromise = full break, but Sparkle refuses any DMG not signed by our key | Mitigated by Sparkle EdDSA ([`UpdaterHost.swift`](../../App/RORORO/Domain/UpdaterHost.swift), [`Info.plist` `SUPublicEDKey`](../../App/RORORO/Info.plist)) |

### Tampering

| Threat | Vector | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DMG modified in transit (CDN compromise, MITM, GitHub Releases breach) | EdDSA signature verified end-to-end by Sparkle; attacker without the private key cannot ship | Mitigated ([`Info.plist` `SUPublicEDKey`](../../App/RORORO/Info.plist), [`tools/release/notarize.sh`](../../tools/release/notarize.sh)) |
| `appcast.xml` modified to point at a malicious DMG | Same: each appcast item carries an EdDSA signature over the DMG; Sparkle fails closed | Mitigated by EdDSA |
| `accounts.json` / `favorites.json` / macro library JSON tampered with on disk by another process | Plain JSON, no signature, no integrity check. Worst case: a tampered macro could inject keystrokes — but only into Roblox windows the user has focused, and the safety monitor will trip if the user moves the mouse | **Accepted** (decided 2026-05-11) — same trust boundary as any user-writable file under `~/Library/Application Support/`. An attacker with write access there has many other attack vectors; HMAC adds Keychain item + load-path complexity without changing the trust model |
| Per-launch Roblox.app copy modified between copy and spawn | We copy then immediately spawn; the window is short but not zero | **Action item** (decided 2026-05-11) — add `codesign --verify --deep --strict` re-check on the copy before each `Process.run`. Catches tampering between copy and spawn. ~50-200ms launch overhead accepted. Note: the `LSMultipleInstancesProhibited` plist flip invalidates the original signature, so the verify will need to happen pre-flip; we're verifying the *original* bytes are valid before we touch them ([`docs/security-audit.md` Findings § "No code-signing of the in-flight per-instance app copies"](../security-audit.md)) |
| FFlag overrides written by `ClientSettingsWriter` corrupted by another process | Plain JSON in the Roblox client's settings dir. If corrupted, Roblox refuses to launch or ignores the flags — fail-open at the Roblox level | **Accepted** — same as any settings file Roblox reads |

### Repudiation

Mostly N/A for a single-user desktop tool. Two narrow cases:

| Threat | Status |
| --- | --- |
| User denies running a macro that violated Roblox ToS | Local Diagnostics bundle includes timestamped recent logs ([`DiagnosticsBundle.swift`](../../App/RORORO/Domain/DiagnosticsBundle.swift)), but logs do not contain cookie values. No central audit trail (intentional — no telemetry per [`PRIVACY.md`](../PRIVACY.md)) |
| User denies which account ran a launch | `accounts.json` `lastLaunched` timestamp + URL-scheme handler logs are local-only. Same posture: no telemetry, repudiation accepted as cost of zero-tracking |

### Information disclosure

The biggest STRIDE category for this app. The cookie is the prize.

| Threat | Vector | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cookie leak via plaintext disk file | Cookies live only in Keychain; `accounts.json` contains only public profile data | Mitigated ([`KeychainStore.swift`](../../App/RORORO/Domain/KeychainStore.swift), [`PRIVACY.md`](../PRIVACY.md)) |
| Cookie leak via iCloud Keychain sync | `kSecAttrSynchronizable: false` — never roams ([`KeychainStore.swift:57`](../../App/RORORO/Domain/KeychainStore.swift)) | Mitigated |
| Cookie leak via crash report / sysdiagnose | We never construct strings that embed cookie values for logging. Cookie is held in plaintext in memory only during a single Launch-As operation ([`docs/security-audit.md` § Cookie storage](../security-audit.md)) | **Accepted** — guarantee is by construction (cookie strings never participate in any `os_log` / `print` / format string). A defensive redaction layer adds complexity without changing a guarantee already enforced at the call sites. Re-verify if any new code path holds a cookie value |
| Cookie leak via diagnostics bundle | `DiagnosticsBundle.writeBundle` copies `accounts.json` + `favorites.json` (no cookies), redacts private-server codes, and includes `log show --process RORORO` — which does not contain cookies because we don't log them ([`DiagnosticsBundle.swift`](../../App/RORORO/Domain/DiagnosticsBundle.swift)) | Mitigated |
| Cookie leak via WKWebView persistence across sessions | `.nonPersistent()` store — cookie store evaporates when the sheet closes ([`CookieCapture.swift:67`](../../App/RORORO/Domain/CookieCapture.swift)) | Mitigated |
| Cookie leak via screen recording / Accessibility tree read by another app | The Accessibility tree of our app exposes window titles and avatar names, not cookie values. A screen recorder sees what's on screen; cookies never render | Mitigated by construction (cookie never rendered) |
| Cross-account bleed inside WKWebView | Today all accounts share a single `.nonPersistent()` store, wiped between sheets | **Low-severity, deferred to v0.2** per [`docs/security-audit.md` Findings § Per-account WKWebView data-store isolation](../security-audit.md) |
| Password capture via fake login | We never see the password — login renders in the embedded `WKWebView` pointed at the real Roblox login URL; only the post-login cookie is captured | Mitigated by design ([`CookieCapture.swift`](../../App/RORORO/Domain/CookieCapture.swift)) |
| Network analytics / telemetry surfacing user identity | No telemetry endpoints. Only HTTPS to Roblox-owned + GitHub-owned hosts ([`PRIVACY.md` § Network connections](../PRIVACY.md)) | Mitigated |
| User-Agent string fingerprinting | We send `RORORO-Mac/<version>` on Roblox API calls — identifies us, not the user. WKWebView keeps default UA so Roblox's login renders correctly ([`CookieCapture.swift:68-70`](../../App/RORORO/Domain/CookieCapture.swift), [`PRIVACY.md`](../PRIVACY.md)) | Accepted — transparent identification, not a leak |

### Denial of service

| Threat | Vector | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sparkle update channel offline (GitHub Pages outage, DNS) | App keeps working; auto-update simply doesn't fire. Manual reinstall is always available | Accepted — graceful degradation |
| `sem_unlink` no-longer-works after Roblox renames `/RobloxPlayerUniq` | `SemaphoreBreaker` silently returns `.alreadyUnlinked` for the unknown name and multi-instance launches start failing ([`SemaphoreBreaker.swift:35-39`](../../App/RORORO/Domain/SemaphoreBreaker.swift)) | **Action item — v0.1.0 blocker** (decided 2026-05-11): ship the Gist-based remote compat-config override that the Windows port has. Closes the gap before any user is affected. Manual workaround until shipped: `strings` recipe in [`docs/runbook/runbook.md` §11.3](../runbook/runbook.md) ([`docs/security-audit.md` Findings § Compat-config remote feed](../security-audit.md)) |
| Accessibility / Input Monitoring permission revoked mid-session | Auto-keys cycler silently no-ops on event-post; safety monitor goes blind. UI surfaces a revoke banner; user has to re-grant | Mitigated by status checks ([`AutoKeysPermissions.swift`](../../App/RORORO/Domain/AutoKeys/AutoKeysPermissions.swift)) |
| Stale URL-scheme handler — RORORO crashes mid-session, scheme stays claimed | Previous handler bundle ID is saved to UserDefaults pre-claim; the next boot can re-restore ([`URLSchemeHandler.swift:32-34`](../../App/RORORO/Domain/URLSchemeHandler.swift)) | Mitigated |
| Sparkle "Install and Relaunch" silent failure with an open SwiftUI sheet | Documented trap; `UpdaterHost.hasUpdateAvailable` flag dismisses sheets before Sparkle's window appears ([`UpdaterHost.swift:22-30`](../../App/RORORO/Domain/UpdaterHost.swift)) | Mitigated |
| Per-instance Roblox copies leaking disk | `RobloxAppCopier.cleanupStaleInstances()` on every boot ([`docs/security-audit.md`](../security-audit.md)) | Mitigated |

### Elevation of privilege

The Accessibility + Input Monitoring grants are themselves elevated privilege relative to a sandboxed app. The concerns are misuse, not bypass.

| Threat | Vector | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Keystrokes posted into the wrong process due to focus race | Multi-window cyclers + workspace observers race; the first focus call can land before pids are tracked. Memory note `feedback_focus_theft_race_pattern.md` documents the pattern: pre-populate trackers before triggering activation events | **Partial** — `WindowFocuser` + `WorkspaceActivationObserver` exist; pre-population was the call-out from `/loop` 2026-05-10. **Real residual risk** — see Residual risks below |
| Cycler keystroke fires after the user Cmd-Tabs away | Safety monitor watches `NSEvent` global streams; non-self-tagged input pauses the cycler. `eventSourceUserData = 0x524F524F` distinguishes our events from the user's ([`EventTapping.swift:23`](../../App/RORORO/Domain/AutoKeys/EventTapping.swift)) | Mitigated for mouse + key activity; **kill-key reliability flagged** per memory note `project_slope_c_auto_keys_in_flight.md` |
| App Sandbox bypass | App Sandbox is OFF by design — multi-instance needs `LSSetDefaultHandlerForURLScheme` + `Process.run("/usr/bin/open")`, both blocked by the sandbox ([`RORORO.entitlements`](../../App/RORORO/RORORO.entitlements), [`docs/security-audit.md`](../security-audit.md)) | Accepted tradeoff |
| Hardened Runtime bypass | Hardened Runtime enforced in Release builds via `project.yml` ([`docs/security-audit.md`](../security-audit.md)) | Mitigated in Release |
| Apple Event automation hijack | No `NSAppleEventsUsageDescription` in `Info.plist`; we don't use Apple Events ([`docs/security-audit.md` Findings § No NSAppleEventsUsageDescription](../security-audit.md)) | Mitigated by not having the entitlement |
| `Process.run` against attacker-controlled path | We only invoke `/usr/bin/open`, `/usr/bin/log`, `/usr/bin/zip` — hardcoded absolute paths, no `$PATH` lookup | Mitigated by hardcoded paths |

## Residual risks

Decisions captured 2026-05-11. The threats below have partial or no mitigation. Each is either explicitly accepted, scheduled for v0.1.0, or carried forward as a known limitation. Re-litigate on the triggers in the next section.

### Accepted

- **Cross-account WKWebView bleed.** Audit's v0.2 priority stands. `.nonPersistent()` already isolates per-launch; real exploit requires same-machine attacker + timing. Re-evaluate at v0.2.
- **Macro-library JSON tampering.** Same trust boundary as any user-writable file under `~/Library/Application Support/`. An attacker with write access there has many other vectors. HMAC adds Keychain + load-path complexity without changing the trust model.
- **Cookie leak via crash report / sysdiagnose.** Guarantee is by construction — cookie strings never participate in `os_log`, `print`, or format strings. A defensive redaction layer would be belt-and-suspenders for a guarantee already enforced at the call sites. Re-verify if any new code path holds a cookie value.

### v0.1.0 ship items

- **Remote compat-config feed for `sem_unlink` name updates.** Port the Windows Gist-based override path to Mac before v0.1.0. Manual workaround until shipped: the `strings` recipe in [`docs/runbook/runbook.md` §11.3](../runbook/runbook.md).
- **Per-launch Roblox.app copy verification.** Add `codesign --verify --deep --strict` on `/Applications/Roblox.app` pre-copy. Pre-copy because the `LSMultipleInstancesProhibited` plist flip invalidates the copy's signature. ~50-200ms launch overhead accepted.
- **Pre-launch URL-scheme handler re-check.** Call `URLSchemeHandler.isClaimed` before each `roblox-player://` launch (not just at startup). Cheap; closes the "malicious app claims scheme mid-session" path.
- **Publish `SECURITY.md` at repo root** with the disclosure policy below.

### Known-bug carry-forward

- **Focus-race when posting keystrokes.** Multi-window cyclers can fire into the wrong window if pid tracking hasn't caught up — flagged in memory note `feedback_focus_theft_race_pattern.md`. **Real bug pattern**, not theoretical. The pre-populate fix is documented; needs to land uniformly across every cycler entry path next session.
- **Kill-key reliability under load.** Memory note `project_slope_c_auto_keys_in_flight.md` flags this for next-session work. The safety monitor sees `NSEvent` streams; under macro load the kill-key gesture can be missed.

### Disclosure policy

90-day private disclosure window. Vulnerabilities reported privately get triaged on the maintainer's schedule; public disclosure follows either a shipped fix or 90 calendar days from initial report, whichever lands first. Good-faith research is welcome; we won't pursue legal action against researchers who report responsibly and don't access more than necessary to demonstrate the issue.

- **Contact:** estevan@626labs.dev.
- **Scope:** the RORORO Mac app and its release pipeline. Out of scope: Roblox Corporation's own infrastructure (report those to Roblox).
- **Out of scope by design:** see [Out of scope / non-goals](#out-of-scope--non-goals).
- A canonical [`SECURITY.md`](../../SECURITY.md) at the repo root captures the same policy in the GitHub-standard location.

### Threat-actor prioritization

Primary and secondary actors only. Mitigations above are tuned for these.

- **Primary — Roblox cheat-vendor / mass distributor.** Low effort, broad reach. Threat model: trojaned binaries impersonating RORORO, phishing pages claiming to be us, harvest-and-replay against many accounts.
- **Secondary — targeted attacker after a specific account.** Limited-inventory holders, popular Roblox creators. Threat model: tailored social engineering, malicious macro distribution, install-time tampering on a specific user's machine.
- **Out of scope — nation-state-grade adversaries.** Not realistic for this product's user base. Mitigations are NOT tuned for this tier.

### Sparkle EdDSA key — incident response

The Sparkle private key is the load-bearing trust root for auto-update. Per [`CLAUDE.md`](../../CLAUDE.md), losing it is a one-way break. Two materially different incidents, two playbooks.

**Scenario A — Key LOST (no attacker access).** Private key destroyed (laptop bricked, 1Password vault wiped, etc.) but no evidence of attacker possession.

1. Generate a new EdDSA keypair offline.
2. Ship one interim release signed with the *old* key whose payload swaps the bundled `SUPublicEDKey` to the new public key. (Sparkle 2.x supports rotation via a signed update that updates the public-key constant.) This requires the old key be at least transiently recoverable; if even one signing operation is possible, use it for the rotation.
3. From that release onward, sign with the new key. Old clients are bridged through the rotation release; no manual user action required.
4. Document the rotation in the release notes and in [`docs/decisions/`](../decisions/).

**Scenario B — Key COMPROMISED (attacker has the private key).** The bridge approach is dead — an attacker can sign anything until we burn the channel.

1. **Burn the appcast immediately.** Replace `https://estevanhernandez-stack-ed.github.io/rororo-mac/appcast.xml` with a static notice page telling users to stop using auto-update and manually re-download from GitHub Releases. Same URL — old Sparkle clients will fetch this and find nothing to update to.
2. **Fork the channel.** New EdDSA keypair; new appcast URL (e.g., `appcast-v2.xml`); new release built fresh from clean infrastructure.
3. **Communicate.** README banner, top-line GitHub Release notes, an `urgent-security.md` doc at the repo root explaining what happened, what users should do, and how to verify the new build (checksum + new EdDSA pubkey published in three independent places).
4. **Rotate everything adjacent.** Apple Developer ID certs (if the compromise vector could have touched them), notarization credentials, gh-pages push token. Treat the breach as "everything on that machine is suspect."
5. **Old clients are stranded.** They cannot auto-update to the new channel — that's the one-way break. They must manually re-download. There is no way to push a signed `please-switch-channels` update if the attacker can also sign one telling them to "switch" to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
6. **Post-incident.** Mortem write-up in [`docs/decisions/`](../decisions/) with what the new key-custody posture is.

## Out of scope / non-goals

These are explicit non-goals, not gaps.

- **Defending against the user attacking themselves.** A user with admin on their own Mac can read their own Keychain by typing their password. That is correct behavior.
- **Defending against another logged-in macOS user reading our login Keychain.** Different login = different Keychain; macOS enforces this.
- **Anti-detection logic, evasion, injection, or patching.** Hard rule per [`CLAUDE.md` § Hard rules](../../CLAUDE.md). `sem_unlink` is the entire mechanism; nothing else.
- **Telemetry-based abuse detection.** No telemetry, full stop. Tradeoff accepted.
- **Server-side protections.** There is no server. All trust is local + Roblox-side.
- **Defending Roblox Corporation's ToS enforcement.** That's between the user and Roblox. We don't help and we don't hinder.
- **Nation-state-grade targeted attacks.** Out of scope per threat-actor prioritization.

## Re-threat-model triggers

Re-run this model (and bump the date) when any of the following land:

- Any change to where cookies are stored.
- Any new network endpoint or any addition of telemetry / analytics / crash reporting.
- Any change to `sem_unlink` posture, per-launch copy flow, or App Sandbox posture.
- A Sparkle key rotation event.
- Addition of any new system-level permission (Apple Events, Full Disk Access, Screen Recording).
- A Roblox-side change that motivates a posture shift around anti-detection (we still wouldn't ship it, but the audit captures why).
- New attack surface from Slope D-onward features (window-management, record-and-replay, macro library) — each ADR should reference this doc if it introduces new event-posting or new permission asks.
